q-138084.name: Question 1
q-138084.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $3.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-138084.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-3I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 1

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−x12+4x1x2+2x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 3. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[−12]
b
113[2−3]
c
15[21]
d
17[31]
e
15[12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−1222]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=3:

A−3I=[−1222]−3[1001]=[−422−1] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−3I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[12].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[12].

q-138128.name: Question 2
q-138128.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=7{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2}-4{x}_{2}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $4.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-138128.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=7x12+8x22+5x32−4x2x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 4. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[011]
b
13[111]
c
12[01−1]
d
12[122]
e
15[012]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[70008−20−25]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=4:

A−4I=[70008−20−25]−4[100010001]=[30004−20−21]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−4I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[012].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umin=v‖v‖=15[012].

q-170414.name: Question 3
q-170414.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}-17{x}_{2}^{2}+7{x}_{3}^{2}-18{x}_{2}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-170414.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -17 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-20)I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -17 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 7\end{aligned}]+20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}19 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 27\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-20)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−x12−17x22+7x32−18x2x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to −20. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
110[103]
b
[301]
c
110[130]
d
110[031]
e
[001]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−1000−17−90−97]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=−20:

A−(−20)I=[−1000−17−90−97]+20[100010001]=[190003−90−927]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−(−20)I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[031].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=10, we get

umin=v‖v‖=110[031].

q-170506.name: Question 4
q-170506.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+16{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when ${x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=4,$ is $20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-170506.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 8 \\ 8 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 8 \\ 8 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 16 \\ 8 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 16 \\ 16 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $20,$ we have

$$
max\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{max}=20.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-20I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 16 \\ 16 & 4\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-16 & 16 \\ 16 & -16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-20I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get  

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

The maximum value of Q(x)=x12+16x1x2+4x22, when x12+4x22=4, is 20. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[−21]
b
110[13]
c
12[21]
d
12[1−1]
e
110[−31]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1884]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1222+x2212=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=2 (along the x1-axis) and b=1 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x12 and y2=x2,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix

P=[2001],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[2001][1884][2001]=[21684][2001]=[416164].

Now, we maximize Q′(y) when ‖y‖=1, as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is 20, we have

max{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmax=20.

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=20:

B−20I=[416164]−20[1001]=[−161616−16] Seeking a non-zero solution of (B−20I)y=0 gives the eigenvector v=[11]. Dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=2, we get

umax=v‖v‖=12[11].

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

xmax=Pumax=[2001]⋅12[11]=12[21]

q-170526.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{4}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=4$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{4},$ 

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -8 \\ -16 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}32 & -32 \\ -32 & -16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}|B-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}32-\lambda  & -32 \\ -32 & -16-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (32-\lambda )(-16-\lambda )-1\,024 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-16\lambda -1\,536 & =0 \\ (\lambda -48)(\lambda +32) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =48,\,-32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
max\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}=48.
$$
